title: Technology Adoption Is Not An Operating Outcome
summary: A five-rail technology-readiness map separating standards, policy, awards, testing, and authorization from deployed, accepted, repeated, and measured operation.
map_question: Which evidence stages separate upstream technology activity from accepted and measured operation across five adoption rails?
interpretation_boundary: The map provides a common stage vocabulary, not a cross-technology ranking or claim of equal maturity, value, safety, performance, or adoption.

nodes.label: Policy, standards, selection, award, or test
nodes.note: A real upstream stage that defines direction, authority, resources, or learning without establishing adoption.

nodes.label: Post-quantum migration
nodes.note: Needs institution-specific inventory, procurement, validation, cutover, acceptance, rollback, and legacy retirement.

nodes.label: AI assurance
nodes.note: Needs named system controls, evaluation, authorization, monitoring, incidents, independent review, and mission outcomes.

nodes.label: Autonomy and eVTOL
nodes.note: Needs certification, local authority, service exposure, safety, availability, accessibility, cost, and repeat outcomes.

nodes.label: Advanced manufacturing
nodes.note: Needs installed equipment, qualification, accepted product, workforce outcomes, yield, downtime, rework, and repeat output.

nodes.label: Critical minerals
nodes.note: Needs facility construction, commissioning, product specifications, qualification, offtake, recycling, and recurring supply.

nodes.label: Accepted deployment or operation
nodes.note: A named authority or receiving system accepts a defined capability, asset, service, product, or transition.

nodes.label: Compatible repeated outcome
nodes.note: Stable identities, definitions, periods, denominators, methods, and acceptance support bounded outcome interpretation.

nodes.label: Three named adoption cases
nodes.note: Phase 61 follows GSA PQC acquisition, NIST ARIA assurance, and Waymo California service into their next named operating artifact.

links.note: Standards and deadlines establish a migration rail without completing it.
Frameworks and pilots create assurance methods without proving operating control effectiveness.
Policy, tests, and pilot selection remain distinct from persistent service.
Roadmaps, awards, and facilities remain upstream of accepted repeat output.
Exposure, programs, and awards remain upstream of qualified material supply.
Completed named-system migrations and accepted transitions remain sparse.
Use cases and pilots exist while comparable assurance and outcome evidence remains incomplete.
Some service authority exists, but persistent exposure and outcome reporting remain uneven.
Named outputs exist for bounded entities without a common or complete production rail.
Selections and projects remain upstream of qualified, accepted, recurring supply.
Acceptance is a prerequisite but still does not establish durable or comparable outcome performance.
Named institutional and operator files expose the exact evidence needed to move from upstream activity toward accepted operation.

what_this_map_supports: Five technology rails can use a common separation between upstream activity, accepted deployment, and measured outcomes.
The most valuable next evidence is attached to named institutions, systems, facilities, operators, products, and receiving authorities.
Adoption dossiers should preserve exact stage and stop-rule language.
DARPA receipt receipt-58-darpa-2026-08-11-no-material-change shows that an elapsed field event can receive a completed no-change decision while measured results and transition evidence remain open.
Phase 61 adds named GSA PQC, NIST ARIA, and Waymo California cases with exact downstream artifacts and stop rules.
Phase 60B receipt receipt-60-darpa-2026-08-23-results closes the measured competition-result gate while leaving maturation, certification, production, service, recurring operation, and outcomes open.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not rank technologies or create readiness, safety, performance, risk, or value scores.
It does not imply equal evidence depth or equivalent deployment conditions.
It does not turn policy, standards, awards, tests, permits, or authorizations into operating outcomes.
next_records_needed: Named institutional PQC inventories, procurements, tests, cutovers, and acceptances.
Named AI system authorizations, monitoring, incidents, independent review, and mission outcomes.
Stable operator-level autonomy and eVTOL service, exposure, safety, accessibility, and cost records, including DARPA's dated Lift Challenge measured-results artifact.
Facility-level manufacturing and critical-minerals qualification, accepted output, and repeated performance.
